newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says it inspired Palestinian movement.
newsitem.headline: Iran says it inspired Palestinian movement.

text.p: Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei said on Friday Iran's militant stand against Israel had inspired Palestinians to continue their fight against the Jewish state.

"The resistance of the Iranian nation (against Israel) has injected fresh blood into the dried veins of the Palestinian movement," Khamenei told a mass audience gathered for Friday prayers at Tehran University.

"If the movement of young Palestinians around the borders and inside occupied Palestine continues then all this peace for which they have sat around tables will turn out meaningless and void and will lead nowhere," he told worshippers.
Iran, which says Israel has no right to exist, has condemned the peace process as a sell-out of Palestinian and Arab rights.
Khamenei, in a rare appearance at Tehran's mass prayers, called on Israel to leave Palestine.
"Iranians shout in one voice that the usurper Zionist state should leave Palestine," he said to the crowd which chanted back "Death to Israel" and "Death to America."
Tehran has denied Israeli and U.S. charges that it has sponsored terrorism, saying it only gives political and moral support to Palestinian groups opposed to the peace accords.
Iran said on Thursday a deal on Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron was only a face-saving move for the United States and other mediators.
